Cryptographically Secure Random Bytes

Source: R/random.R
crypt_rand_bytes.Rd

Draws n bytes from the operating system's cryptographic random source: rand_s on Windows, arc4random_buf on macOS and the BSDs, getrandom on Linux with glibc 2.25 or later, and /dev/urandom elsewhere. crypt_info() names the one compiled in, in build_flags$random_backend. Use these bytes for keys, initialisation vectors, nonces and salts.

Usage

crypt_rand_bytes(n = 1)

Arguments

n

The number of bytes: a single non-negative whole number. n = 0 returns raw(0).

Value

A raw vector of length n.

Details

R's random number generator is never involved. set.seed() has no effect on these bytes and they do not change .Random.seed, so drawing them does not disturb a reproducible simulation running beside them. That is deliberate: R's generator is seeded from the session and reproducible on purpose, which is exactly what a key must not be.

The name, argument and default mirror openssl::rand_bytes(), so code moving from openssl changes only the prefix.

Errors

A failure of the operating-system source raises an error of class zucrypt_entropy_error. It never returns fewer bytes than asked for, and never returns bytes from a source that reported failure. An invalid n is zucrypt_invalid_argument.

See also

crypt_aes_cbc_encrypt_nopad(), whose iv for encryption must be unpredictable: crypt_rand_bytes(16) is one.

Examples

crypt_rand_bytes(16)
#>  [1] 48 11 e1 a5 7e 92 df e5 8d 43 20 33 f3 93 45 8a

# A 256-bit key, printed as hex.
crypt_hex(crypt_rand_bytes(32))
#> [1] "70efa3e4564a458bc2f97f003cf8f984e4fbb55ee9a0f4b95800d085b5977b06"

# set.seed() does not repeat it.
set.seed(1)
a <- crypt_rand_bytes(8)
set.seed(1)
b <- crypt_rand_bytes(8)
identical(a, b)
#> [1] FALSE
